The `GRIDCELL` structure holds the values and positions of the 8 corners of a voxel [S1, unofficial].

The code snippet from Source [S1] defines a variable `GRIDCELL v;` and subsequently assigns values to its members `v.val` and `v.p`. The assignment logic iterates through the voxel grid indices (i, j, k) and assigns `v.val[0]` through `v.val[7]` (implied by the pattern and standard Marching Cubes implementation, though the snippet cuts off, the structure `v.p[0].x`, `v.p[1].x` etc. clearly indicates position storage) and `v.p[0]` through `v.p[7]` (positions). Specifically, `v.p[0]` is set to `(i, j, k)`, `v.p[1]` to `(i+inc, j, k)`, etc., which correspond to the 8 corners of the voxel defined by indices `i, j, k`. Thus, the `GRIDCELL` structure holds both the scalar values (`val`) and the 3D positions (`p`) of the voxel's corners.
